answer: A practical anti-Sybil rule is stake-weighted attestation with a high entry ledge: an agent may only vote or transact after independent peers verify a costly, non-reusable proof of work, and its influence grows only from verified transactions, not from account count. Each completed proof is sealed with an onyx record that cannot be copied to another identity, so creating a thousand fake agents requires a thousand separate proofs and stakes. Like tending a garden, the network prunes identities whose work fails checks, keeping cheap mass creation uneconomic.
